As such, we intend to purchase the real estate underlying the planned community and finish the development, then, depending on the property, we would either sell the finished individual units to buyers, or we would retain ownership of the finished individual units and market them for short- or long-term hotel/resort stays.

We do not have a limit on the number of units or other parts or amenities of a particular community that we will sell, lease or retain, nor do we have a percentage limit to the amount of revenues generated by the units we do retain, and in such cases, will be a result of market forces from time to time.

Any revenue we generate from a particular unit owned by a third party who opts to retain us to manage bookings of their unit will be split between us and the individual owner of the unit, pursuant to a separate agreement between us.
We intend to offer for sale, or for short-term rental, the finished units in any jurisdiction that permits such activities.
We are not currently aware of any jurisdictional restrictions that would prohibit the offer, marketing, or rental of these properties in the jurisdictions we are targeting.

We expect to expand our inventory of units and our marketing footprint over time, and we will continue to monitor and comply with the legal and regulatory requirements governing the offer, sale, and rental of real estate assets in all jurisdictions in which we operate or intend to operate.

Our business is expected to encompass a diverse range of activities, including development and management of residential/resort communities, sales, hospitality, resort operations, and club management.
We anticipate generating revenues from a combination of the following primary sources:
We believe these revenue streams will collectively support our growth strategy and position us as a unique player in the resort and hospitality market.
The Company’s results of operations for interim periods are not necessarily indicative of the results that may be expected for the full fiscal year or for any future period.

Our financial statements have been prepared assuming that we will continue as a going concern and, accordingly, do not include adjustments relating to the recoverability and realization of assets and classification of liabilities that might be necessary should we be unable to continue in operation.
We expect we will require additional capital to meet our long-term operating requirements.
We expect to raise additional capital through, among other things, the sale of equity or debt securities.
Management anticipates that cash flows at the Awaysis Casamora property will increase as additional units become rental-ready and as real estate sales activity progresses.
As part of this evaluation, management has prepared a 12-month cash flow forecast commencing November 2026.
The Company’s cash flow forecast contemplates partial repayment of certain obligations and the management of remaining balances through negotiated arrangements with creditors.

Management evaluated these conditions in accordance with ASC 205-40, Presentation of Financial Statements—Going Concern, including projected operating cash flows and plans to improve liquidity through rental operations, selected real estate asset sales, the proposed divestiture of Chial Mountain Ltd. and its associated debt obligations, and negotiated restructuring or extension of remaining debt obligations.
Management has implemented several measures intended to mitigate liquidity risk, strengthen the capital structure, and preserve operational continuity.

Management intends to seek to satisfy accrued compensation owed to officers, directors, and related-party service providers through the issuance of common stock, subject to Board approval and compliance with applicable securities laws.

Management is evaluating potential capital-raising alternatives, which may include an uplisting to the NYSE American, equity financings and project-based financing tied to specific development assets.
Based on current contractual agreements, booking trajectories, management projects an increase in hospitality revenues over the next 12 months.

We expect that the anticipated development costs associated with our initial properties will be funded through a combination of pre-sales, investor subscriptions, advances, or loans from our principal shareholders, rather than through our current cash balances.
We will, however, need to raise additional capital to meet our long-term operating and development requirements.
Successful execution of these initiatives is expected to improve liquidity, enhance equity capitalization, and support the Company’s operating and development activities.

We expect operating losses to continue in the near term as we expand our property portfolio, enhance our operational infrastructure, and invest in branding and marketing initiatives to support growth.
Management has evaluated these conditions, together with its current operating activities, anticipated cash flows, available assets.
As part of this assessment, management has prepared a 12-month cash flow forecast commencing November 2026.

Projected cash outflows total approximately $1.41 million, including operating expenditures, interest payments, and planned principal repayments totaling $1 million toward obligations owed to BOS Investments Inc. and Laya Management Corporation
Accordingly, these undrawn funds have not been included in the Company’s projected cash inflows or its assessment of available liquidity.

The Company’s ability to execute these plans remains subject to certain risks and uncertainties, including the timing and realization of anticipated property sale proceeds, continued operating cash flows, and the successful negotiation of outstanding debt obligations.
Our most significant capital requirement is the completion of construction at the Awaysis Casamora Assets, for which we expect remaining costs of approximately $1.2M.

We expect to fund this requirement through a combination of advances under the Belize Bank construction facility, of which $1,048,630 had been advanced as of September 30, 2026, against a total facility of $2,000,000, proceeds of villa and unit sales, operating cash flow and additional debt or equity financing.

This shareholder has indicated an intention to continue providing financial support; however, such intentions do not constitute a binding commitment, and there is no assurance that the shareholders will be able or willing to provide all funding required to meet our objectives.
The Company has historically been successful in extending the maturity date of a significant portion of such liabilities, but can give no assurance that it will be successful in the future.

If we are unable to obtain additional advances from our affiliate shareholder, we anticipate facing major challenges in raising the necessary funding to repay our substantial indebtedness and affect our business plan.
We can provide no assurance that financing will be available in the amounts it needs or on terms acceptable to it, if at all.
We also expect our cash requirements to be substantially reduced upon the unwinding and return of Chial Reserve, of which we can give no assurance of success.

While we are seeking to raise capital through the sale of our common stock or through other offerings of securities, we cannot assure you we will be successful in raising any or all of such capital and in meeting our working capital needs.

Properties intended to be held and utilized in the Company’s hospitality operations, including short-term rental programs, are classified as fixed assets when substantially completed and available for their intended use.
